Chapter 9. Challenges and Questions: Walking the Path with Honesty.
Let’s be real—no journey of faith is ever completely smooth. And as more people embrace the devotion to the Divine Heart of God the Father, it’s only natural that some tough questions and honest worries pop up along the way.
Some folks wonder if this new devotion might take the spotlight away from Christ, or maybe even muddle our understanding of the Trinity itself. And for others, just the word “father” can bring up old wounds—painful memories that make it hard to connect.
I remember a parish meeting where these feelings really came to the surface. There was a woman—her voice shaking a little—who shared how calling God “Father” brought back memories of hurt and disappointment. The priest didn’t rush in with easy solutions. Instead, he just listened. He let her know her pain was real, and gently invited her to imagine the Father’s heart as something different—something that could actually heal, instead of hurt.
Then someone else asked if this devotion is truly “official”—does it have the Church’s blessing? The priest explained that the Votive Mass was created with careful attention, deeply rooted in the Church’s traditions and always faithful to her teachings. He encouraged everyone to keep an open heart, trusting that the Spirit would guide them.
Of course, there are practical challenges, too. At first, the prayers and new rituals might feel strange, maybe even a little awkward. It takes a while for a community to find its rhythm—to let the new become familiar. There are moments when people miss the comfort of what’s always been. But with time, those unfamiliar prayers can become sources of real strength.
This path isn’t always easy. There are setbacks, misunderstandings, and moments where doubt creeps in. But here’s what’s inspiring—the community learns to walk together, patiently, gently supporting one another. Every challenge is a chance to grow and to trust a little more deeply in the Father’s love.
And maybe that’s the most important thing. Facing these tough questions honestly helps everyone realize the journey itself matters just as much as where we’re headed. Devotion to the Divine Heart of God the Father isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about being willing to seek, to wrestle with questions, and to trust. It’s a path marked by humility, openness, and hope.
